title: Route 53 Routing Policies & Health Checks
summary: DNS-based failover, weighting and latency routing for multi-AZ and multi-Region designs.
tldr: Route 53 routing policies decide **which** answer a DNS query gets: failover, weighted, latency, geolocation, geoproximity, multivalue, IP-based or simple.
Attach **health checks** (or set **Evaluate Target Health** on alias records) so Route 53 stops returning unhealthy endpoints.
Use **alias records** for AWS targets (ALB, CloudFront, S3 website, API Gateway). They work at the zone apex and queries to AWS resources are free.
DNS failover depends on client TTLs. When the question says *don't depend on DNS changes* or wants a manual, safe switch, use **ARC routing controls** (or Global Accelerator).

keyFacts.text: Route 53 health checkers run on the internet and can't reach private IPs. For private resources, check a **CloudWatch alarm** instead.
A **calculated health check** combines other health checks, for example "healthy if at least 2 of 3 children are healthy".
**Multivalue answer** routing returns up to eight healthy records per query. It is simple client-side load spreading, not a load balancer.
**Weighted** records split traffic by each weight's share of the total. Use them for canary releases and gradual migrations; weight 0 stops traffic unless every other record is unhealthy.
**Geoproximity** routing grows or shrinks a Region's geographic area with a bias value instead of listing countries.

traps: A **CNAME can't be created at the zone apex**. Use an alias record.
**Simple routing** with several values does no health checking, so it can't fail over.
Latency-based routing picks the fastest Region, not the closest country. Use geolocation when the rule is about *where the user is*.
Geolocation with no **default** record returns no answer for users in locations you didn't map.
Raising a health check's failure threshold to avoid false failovers still leaves failover automatic. If people must decide, use ARC routing controls.
Adding Route 53 health-checker IP ranges to a security group doesn't help a private-only endpoint. The checkers can't route to private IPs.
Global Accelerator traffic dials and ARC routing controls move traffic without waiting for DNS caches. Editing weighted records does not.

sections.heading: Health check types
sections.body:
- **Endpoint** check: HTTP, HTTPS or TCP against a public IP or domain name, optionally matching a string in the response.
- **Calculated** check: combines child checks with AND, OR or "at least N healthy".
- **CloudWatch alarm** check: healthy while the alarm is OK. Use it for private resources or any custom metric.
- On an **alias** record that targets an AWS resource, turn on **Evaluate Target Health** instead of creating a separate check.
